findings.where: Article specimen: the subheads "So, what are the key ‘chapter topics’?" and "Download", at both widths
findings.fault: The subheads are set in a heavy, wide black grotesque. It is neither of the tile's two faces: the type pair says subheads are Newsreader 500. It adds a third typeface that shouts. Beside the quiet Newsreader text and the light serif hero, it reads as a slick tech-startup heading, not a legal journal.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose brief asks for serious, refined type with nothing 'in-your-face techy', and who wants the article page to carry the tile's look. A development-bank reader also meets a voice on the article page that the homepage never used, so the site feels pieced together.

findings.where: Article specimen: the title "The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law", at both widths
findings.fault: The title is set in a heavy, tightly packed bold serif. That weight appears nowhere in the stated system, which is Light 300 for display, 400 for text and 500 for subheads, and it clashes with the light, airy display line that is the tile's signature on the first screen. The homepage whispers and the article page shouts, so the two surfaces don't read as one hand.
findings.who_objects: The founder, judging whether this direction holds together from homepage to article (Counsel's paper is meant to read as 'the editorial gravitas of a legal journal'). Angélique will also have two conflicting heading styles to copy when she adds articles.
